title: The neuron, driven hard and gently

data.source: Allen Institute for Brain Science, Allen Cell Types Database (celltypes.brain-map.org): long square sweeps of the first 60 mouse and first 30 human cells by specimen id
data.licence: Allen Institute Terms of Use (research and non-commercial use with citation; not Creative Commons)

claim_kind: retrodiction (published recordings; mapping frozen before any spike count was looked at)
prediction: The charge a neuron takes in per spike is the same at every current: the median over cells of the slope of log(charge per spike) on log(current) has a 95 % interval inside -0.05 to +0.05.
baseline: The field's own model (leaky integrate-and-fire with each cell's measured rheobase: charge per spike falls as current rises) and a clock decoy (a fixed firing pace, slope +1).
why: Charge per spike changed with the current by more than the band allows; a neuron is not a fixed-count counter of injected charge. Nearest of the three rules: the field's leaky model. Rider from the second check: only the sign is robust. The size depends on which sweeps are kept, the close match to the leaky model holds only under the frozen selection, and charge above rheobase per spike is not flat either. This is `fails` for the frozen reading "the input is the count". The second checker argues, by hand and unverified, that CRR's rule R4 predicts the same leak as the leaky model, which would make it `restates`.

first_run.note: unchanged by the second check; a rider was added

amended.reason:
AMENDMENT, 2026-11-19, AFTER THE SECOND CHECK (docs/CHECKS_RATE_SECOND_LOOK.md). The frozen docstring, the verdict
`fails` and every first-run number are unchanged. A rider is added at the second checker's request.
(1) Only the SIGN is robust. The size depends on which sweeps are kept: the second checker found the median slope
running from about -2.1 (every spiking sweep) to -0.30 (currents spanning a factor of two), on the same table.
(2) The agreement of the leaky model's median with the measured median to 0.01 holds only under the frozen
selection. Cell by cell the gap is far larger; this script now reports it.
(3) Charge ABOVE RHEOBASE per spike, (I - I_rh) x D / (N + 0.5), is not flat either; it rises with current. This
script now reports that slope on the frozen sweeps.
(4) THE SECOND CHECKER'S READING, done by hand and NOT verified here or against Phoenix code: CRR's rule R4
(drive minus a restoring force) gives drive delivered per cut = integral of zeta x tau / (tau - U_s) ds, which
has a stall drive and falls toward a floor as drive grows; with zeta = C, tau = I, U_s = V/R it is the leaky
integrate-and-fire equation. On that reading CRR with R4 predicts the same leak as the field, and the verdict
would be `restates`. The frozen claim here was R2 with R3 read plainly, "the input is the count", and for that
claim `fails` stands.
